title: What An Audience Member Actually Does
objective: Name what an audience member notices, and say why noticing is the evidence a review is built on.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Week 4. Trinity Arts Award Bronze. What An Audience Member Actually Does.
Objective: name what an audience member notices, and say why noticing is the evidence a review is built on.
Success evidence: four notices on your frame sheet, each naming one choice and what it did, with one ringed.

Everything you notice comes from the approved pack or from work put in front of you. You talk about the work: colour, scale, material, sound. You are never asked about your home, your family, your body, how you look or what you believe. Nobody in this room is asked what they believe. Identity here means what you as a maker keep choosing, read off artwork and never off a life.
Nothing is booked. The event is not named yet. We may go to them. They may come to us. We may meet live on screen. An online exhibition counts too. The job in this deck is the same either way.
40 minutes. Offline.

This deck evidences Bronze Part B, Explore the arts as an audience member. The register says Part B requires attending at least one arts event or experience, reflecting on quality and creative impact, and views shared with at least one other person, evidenced. The register also notes that an online exhibition is legitimate. This deck is the preparation for that part and asserts no attendance: no event, venue or date is named anywhere in it, and it runs unchanged whether we go to them, they come to us, or we meet live on screen. Bronze attempted rule, in the register's words: ONE Attempted allowed overall. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The evidence file cap is 10 files for the whole Bronze level, so today's frame sheet joins the Part B file rather than opening a new one. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication.

Delivery is through a validated centre; confirm local validation and an adviser trained at Bronze before assessment. Neither is asserted as completed here. Core, Extend and Challenge are support routes inside Bronze, not different awards. The prompts and sample quantities are teaching scaffolds, not extra assessment requirements. Scribe only the pupil’s own words. Store evidence by part; one cumulative file per part is a suggested four-file plan within the ten-file cap.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Frame sheets and approved pack cards out on desks before pupils sit. One card each, face up, nothing handed round mid-stage.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil turns a notice onto home, family, faith or how somebody looks, say: give me the colour and the size instead. Then write down what they say.

blocks.text: An audience member has a job
So far you have been the maker.
You made work and you improved a skill.
Today you swap sides.
You become the audience member.
An audience member does more than look.
Notice a choice and record it by speech, sketch or writing.
A notice names one choice the maker made.
Then it says what that choice did.
You need three things: your frame sheet, one pencil and one card from the approved pack.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Read both accounts yourself. Do not ask a pupil to model the poor one.

blocks.text: Two visitors, one room
Two people go to the same room of work.
The first walks the whole room in four minutes.
They pass thirty works and name none.
Later they write three words: it was good.
The second stays with one work for four minutes.
They write that the blue is darker at the bottom.
Then they write what it did: my eye sank.
Now think about the review each one owes.
The first has nothing to build on.
The second has a choice and an effect.

items: Seeing is passing your eyes over a work.
Noticing is naming one choice you can point at.
Evidence is that notice, written down at the time.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Model one card only. Keep your own notice to two lines so pupils copy the size of it, not your style. For preparation, draw or project the exact simple example described here, and label it a made-up practice work. Do not attribute its features to an unrelated artwork.

blocks.text: I notice one work, out loud
Watch me notice, using one card from the approved pack.
Step one is stop. I stay with one work.
I count to twenty before I write.
Step two is name. I name one choice I can see.
I say that a thick dark border fills the edge of the card.
That is a choice about line, tone and composition.
Step three is effect. I say what the choice did.
I say that the dark border draws my eye to the pale centre.

blocks.caption: Four steps, and one notice is finished
blocks.title: The four steps of a notice
blocks.alt: Boxes labelled STOP, NAME, EFFECT, WRITE. Four steps, and one notice is finished

blocks.text: Step four is write. I write both parts now.
A quick note can help you recall the detail later.
Notice the words I did not use.
I did not say nice, boring or amazing.
These views need a detail from the work to explain them.
Say the four step names out loud as you do them: stop, name, effect, write. The steps are the thing being taught here, not the card you happen to hold.

stages.title: We Do · label and explain
stages.data-ta1: Use the model activity, then transfer the idea to the learner’s own work. Allow speech, pointing or a scribe.

data.heading: Label a choice, then add your view
data.instruction: Label the craft choice in each panel. Then annotate one panel: say what you notice and what it does for you. You do not have to like it.

categories.label: Scale: the size of a shape

items.label: Label panel A
items.feedback: Two colours meet at an edge. You can name the choice, then give your own response.

items.label: Label panel B
items.feedback: The circles have the same colour but different sizes. Scale is the size choice.

data.discussion: Point to one detail. Tell a partner its effect on you. They may see it differently. Add a short label or spoken note with your reason.
data.staffNote: The labels describe observable choices. Effects and preferences are personal; do not mark a different supported response wrong. This drawing rehearses noticing, not participation in a real audience experience.

stages.data-ta2: The labels describe observable choices. Effects and preferences are personal; do not mark a different supported response wrong. This drawing rehearses noticing, not participation in a real audience experience.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Show the fast sweep once, at speed, so the fault is seen and not only described.

blocks.text: One work close beats thirty works fast
Now watch the same room done the wrong way.
I walk fast and I look at everything.
At the end I write it was good.
Those three words cannot be reviewed.

boxes.head: ONE WORK, CLOSE
boxes.line2: the effect written at the time

blocks.caption: Same room, and only one visit leaves evidence
blocks.title: Close against fast
blocks.alt: Boxes labelled ONE WORK, CLOSE, THIRTY WORKS, FAST. Same room, and only one visit leaves evidence

blocks.text: Part B asks you about quality and creative impact.
Quality needs a choice to hang on.
Impact needs an effect you felt.
So the rule is fixed: one work at a time.
Four notices fill a sheet. Thirty glances fill none.
Write at the time, not on the way home.
Use a pencil, a phone note, or an adult who writes for you.

items: 1 · pick one work and stay with it.
2 · name one choice you can point at.
3 · say what that choice did to you.
4 · write both parts before you move on.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Pair by table, not by choice. Call the swap out loud at two minutes.

blocks.text: Try one notice with a partner
Work in twos, with one pack card between you.
Partner one gives a notice out loud.
It must have a choice and an effect.
Partner two checks it with one question.
The question is: what can I point at?
If nothing can be pointed at, it is an opinion.
Then partner one says it again with a choice in it.
Swap over, with two minutes each way.
You may give your honest view. Add a detail to explain it.
If you get stuck, name a colour first.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Write words down for any pupil who asks. Copy what they said and do not upgrade the sentence.
stages.data-ta2: Watch for a sheet filling with feelings only. Tap the choice box and ask what can I point at.

blocks.text: Four notices on your frame sheet
Now work on your own.
Take one card from the approved pack.
Write four notices on your frame sheet.
Each notice fills two boxes.
Box one is the choice you can point at.
Box two is what that choice did.
Label each choice: colour, scale, material or sound.
Use the labels that fit the work. Do not invent a sound or material you cannot check.
Then ring the notice you would put in a review.
A good ring names a choice and an effect.
A weak ring names only a feeling.
Nothing is booked yet, so these are practice notices.
The same frame works whatever the route turns out to be.

items: Core · Use the labels to notice a craft choice and its effect. Say your view to an adult and record whom, how and where the record is saved.
Extend · write four notices, label each choice, and ring the strongest.
Challenge · as Extend, and write why that one is the strongest.

blocks.text: If you finish early, write one question for the maker.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: The named adult writes the pupil's words, not a tidier version, then records whom and how and the date in front of them.

blocks.text: Say one notice to an adult
Read your ringed notice to the adult at your table.
They write it on your sheet in your words.
Record their name or role, how you shared, and today's date.
That adult is your audience today.
Keep a record of whom you shared with and how.
A note or a short sound or video clip can record the share.
The sheet goes in your Part B folder.
Write the file name on it before it is filed.
Now pick one thing that happens next. Keep the frame, add a fifth notice, or change the one you ringed.
Write your pick under the date.

The register refuses in arts log as an evidence locator: it wants the file name plus the page, slide or timecode. Make sure the file name is on the sheet before it leaves the room, or this share cannot be located at moderation.
Add this work to your Part B file. Write the file name and page number. For a sound or video clip, give the file name and the time where your evidence starts.
This is a practice share from the pack. Label it preparation. Part B is completed after the real arts experience, its review and its share.

print.intro: Write each notice in two boxes on this sheet, the choice you can point at first and what it did second. You may speak, point or write; keep your own words in the record.
focusRows: One choice named that another person could point at in the work
What that choice did, written in the box next to it
One notice ringed, with a record of who received it and how and today's date
tiers: Use the labels to notice a craft choice and its effect. Say your view to an adult and record whom, how and where the record is saved.
Write four notices in two boxes each, label the choices, and ring the strongest.
As Extend, and write one sentence saying why that notice is the strongest.
checks: Each notice names a choice a reader could point at in the work.
Each notice says what that choice did, in the pupil's own words.
Each choice carries a label: colour, scale, material or sound.
One notice is ringed and has a record of the recipient, method, date and file plus page or timecode.
The evidence locator gives the actual file name plus page, slide or timecode.
